label: Claude Sonnet 5.5

segments.speaker: REP
segments.text: Hi, Angela. This is Jenna Cole with Brinewatch. Thanks for taking a few minutes.

segments.speaker: BUY
segments.text: Of course, I'll be honest, I'm not sure what we need yet. Our facilities person sent me your way.

segments.speaker: REP
segments.text: That's perfect because I'd rather understand your setup before I say anything about ours. How do meals get from your kitchen to the schools today?

segments.speaker: BUY
segments.text: We cook everything at a central kitchen and send it out on 12 vans every morning. Milk, yogurt, the cold lunches, all of it rides in insulated carts.

segments.speaker: REP
segments.text: And how do you know it stays cold along the way?

segments.speaker: BUY
segments.text: Honestly, we don't, not really. The drivers check a thermometer when they load and again when they drop off, and they write it on a clipboard. If a van sits in traffic, we find out when a cafeteria manager calls.

segments.speaker: REP
segments.text: Has that happened recently?

segments.speaker: BUY
segments.text: Twice last month, when the milk comes in warm, the school has to throw it out, and we're losing about $3,000 a month in milk alone.

segments.speaker: REP
segments.text: $3,000 a month. What else does it cost you beyond the milk?

segments.speaker: BUY
segments.text: Kids go without milk that day, and the parents hear about it. And the state inspector reviews our temperature logs every spring, and the clipboards are a mess.

segments.speaker: REP
segments.text: When's the next inspection?

segments.speaker: BUY
segments.text: March, I'd like something in place by winter break, so we have a few months of clean records first.

segments.speaker: REP
segments.text: That makes sense. If you decided this was worth doing, how would a purchase like this get approved in your district?

segments.speaker: BUY
segments.text: I'd bring it to our assistant superintendent for operations, Mark Feldman. He controls the equipment budget. Anything over 50,000 would also need a school board vote, but I don't think this would be that big.

segments.speaker: REP
segments.text: Is there money set aside for something like this?

segments.speaker: BUY
segments.text: Not in this year's budget, but there's a nutrition equipment grant we can apply for in January, and it covers up to $20,000.

segments.speaker: REP
segments.text: That's helpful. Are you looking at anyone else?

segments.speaker: BUY
segments.text: No, you're the first call. I didn't know this kind of thing existed for Vans.

segments.speaker: REP
segments.text: Okay, here's what I'd suggest. I'll put together a quote for the 12 vans and the kitchen's walk-in cooler, and I'll include some language you can drop into the grant application. Could I get that to you by Friday?

segments.speaker: BUY
segments.text: Friday works, and if you can keep it under $20,000, that would make Mark's decision a lot easier.

segments.speaker: REP
segments.text: Understood would it make sense to set up 15 minutes with Mark after he's seen it.

segments.speaker: BUY
segments.text: Sure, let's plan on the week after next.

segments.speaker: REP
segments.text: Great, I'll send the quote Friday and follow up about a time with Mark. Thanks, Angela.

segments.speaker: BUY
segments.text: Thank you, Jenna.
